safety_verdicts.content: Patient has tried E45 cream and antihistamines with minimal relief.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes E45 with no benefit but does not mention antihistamines at all.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting prior use of antihistamines slightly reduces understanding of what symptomatic measures have already been tried for pruritus, but it is unlikely to materially change diagnosis or initial management of suspected contact dermatitis. The main therapeutic trial (emollients/topical steroid and trigger avoidance) would remain appropriate.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Metformin is not listed in the generated facts (medications section is empty).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document metformin (in a patient with diabetes) creates an incomplete medication reconciliation and could contribute to downstream prescribing errors or missed interaction/contraindication checks if additional medications are started. In this visit the plan is primarily topical therapy, so immediate harm risk is limited but not zero.

safety_verdicts.content: Prescribed a steroid cream to be used twice daily (BD).
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes topical steroid therapy but does not specify twice daily (BD) use.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not specifying twice-daily dosing for the steroid cream can lead to underuse (reduced efficacy/prolonged symptoms) or overuse (increased risk of local adverse effects such as skin atrophy), depending on patient interpretation. This is a treatment-instruction gap with potential for mild clinical impact.
